Mr. Harendra Nath Nondy, Advocate ----- for the defendant-petitioners
Mr. Nurul Amin, with Mrs. Sakila Rowshan, Advocates ----- for the opposite party No. 1
parties:
Janab Ali Mondal and others
Vs.
Md. Anowar Hossain and others
full_judgment:
9. Mr. Amin next submits that Exhibit-1, the C.S. Khatian bears the name of Kunja Behari Ghose as a Rayoti Tenant which cannot be surrendered simply by oral pronouncement without compliance of the provisions of sections 85, 86 and 87 of the Bengal Tenancy Act. Thus the statement of Rashik Lal P.W.4 as to surrendering the tenancy by his predecessor to the superior Landlord cannot be construed as complete evidence and as such the petitioner cannot take any advantage of the said statement. Mr. Amin submits that the court below very carefully considered all the evidences on record specially Exhibit-'A' series the rent receipts and came to proper finding that the defendants failed to prove their title no matter Goddai Molla's name was in the record for a certain period but without filing any rent receipt or any other document his title is not proved. Lastly, Mr. Amin submits that for argument sake if it is found that the plaintiffs title through his predecessor's settlement in 1350 B.S. is not valid, which is not at all admitted rather found to be proved as valid by the last court of fact, even then possessing the suit property since 1350 B.S. as proved by P.Ws. and found by both of the courts below, the plaintiff has a good and valid title by way of adverse possession and the plaintiff had been enjoying the same and also transferred some portion of it to different persons and now he is possessing the rest of it along with 3 Khathas of his paternal property. In support of his contention he relied on the case of Sadak Ali Vs. Suruj Ali and other reported in 7 DLR 94 and on case of Sheikh Abdul Majid and others Vs. Dhudar Chandra Chose and others reported in 16 DLR 287. Thus according to him the judgment of the court of appeal below having been based on proper consideration and appreciation of all the material evidences available on record and upon proper scrutinizing the same, is a correct judgment and as such there is nothing to interfere with the same. 

 11. It appears from the record that the plaintiff produced five witnesses and some documentary evidences to prove his case and relying upon all the evidences on record and considering the same the courts below disbelieved the title of Godai Molla as the defendants failed to produce or prove the alleged "Bondabasta Nama" and also failed to prove the date of settlement by Kunja Behar' in favour of Godai Molla or any other date of settlement subsequent thereto by the superior Landlord Raja Promatha Nath Roy as alleged, by producing any oral or documentary evidence nor the defendants filed any evidence to prove that Godai or his successors, ever paid rents to the Landlord before transferring the property to the present defendants. Documents they have produced in this respect is Exhibit-`A' series which show that some rents were paid by one Ainuddin a non-contesting defendant having no interest in the suit land to the Government amongst which the earliest receipt is found to be dated 17.7.1981 which is subsequent to the institution of the present suit though shown to have been paid for the years 1379-83 B.S. and the other receipts are of different dates during the pendency of the suit not prior to that. As such there is no evidence on record from which the courts below could arrive at a decision that Godai Molla had a valid title and after his death his heirs inherited the same and transferred it to the defendants. On the contrary the plaintiff's title through Rashik Lal, son of Kunja Behari Ghose, the admitted C.S. recorded tenant of the suit and, has been proved by Rashik Lal himself as P.W.4. On perusing Exhibit 1 and 2 series it appears that after Kunja Behari Ghose his son and successor Rashik Lal himself as P.W.4 became the owner of the suit land and continued to possess the same and settled the same to the plaintiff on receiving rents from him. Exhibit 2 series, the rent receipts of 1350 to 1357 B.S. received by Rashik Lal having been produced before the Court and admitted by Rashik Lal, clearly show that there is no discrepancy in this respect that the suit land has been transferred to the plaintiff who paid rents to Rashik Lal. Relying on the case of Safar Mia and other Vs. Ajufannessa and others reported in 22 DLR 259 it can very well be said that when no less than the settler himself i.e. in this case Rashik Lal, the son of the admitted recorded tenant Kunija Behari, appears and admits the rent receipts then the primary of the same is already made and the burden of proving contrary or otherwise of those receipts thereafter is thus shifted to the persons who challenges the same. In Md. Yasin's case reported in 2 BCR 16 it has also been held that there is no dispute on the proposition that the onus to prove the tenancy lies heavily on the persons who claim the same. In the present case the onus of proving the transfer from the admitted tenant Kunja Behari Ghose through his son Rashik Lal Ghose to the plaintiff lies on the plaintiff and to prove the same the plaintiff produced Rashik Lal himself who proved that on the demise of Kunja Behari, he as his son, transferred the property to the plaintiff in 1350 B.S. on receipt of rents. He proved the rent receipts, Exhibit-2 series in support of his contention which are the documents showing payment of rent for the years 1350, 1352, 1354 and 1357 B.S. respectively. The signatures in those receipts dakhilas having been proved by Rashik Lal himself, those are rightly taken into consideration by the court of appeal below which decree the suit. Though the defendant petitioners tried to draw some contradictions in the genuinely of those rent receipts by cross examining P.W.6 one Sanaullah but surprisingly Rashik Lal the person claiming to have signed the said dakhilas have not been cross examined on the validity of the same. Thus it appears that the plaintiff proved the transfer in his favour by sufficient evidence. It appears that admittedly, nothing has been produced by the defendants before the court to prove Godai's title by way of settlement by Kunja Behari Ghose or the superior Landlord nor any evidence has been led to prove payment of rent from Godai time till filing of the suit in 1980 to prove that Godai Molla or any of the subsequent transferees paid rents in support of their title or possession in the suit land except Exhibit-'A' sense which is subsequent to institution of the suit which has already discussed earlier. However, in no manner the said rent receipts prove that Godai or his successors had title or paid rent in the suit property or that the present set of defendant except Ainuddin, ever paid rents. Thus such rent receipts paid by another person who is subsequent to the institution of the suit cannot be considered as corollary evidence of title and possession of the defendants and as such, the 35 DLR case, in any view of the matter, does not come to any assistance to the defendant petitioners. Thus in the absence of any such evidence on record the courts below rightly found that Godai and or the defendants claim through him do not have any title in the suit land. 

 12. The question of surrendering or abandoning the settlement to the superior Land-lord by Kunja Behari Ghose, a reaiyat, though stated by P.W. 4 Rashik Lal, if found to be correct even then the same cannot be construed to have been done in accordance with the provisions of law because the provisions of sections 85, 86 and 87 of the Bengal Tenancy Act has not been complied with. Though Rashik Lal stated that his father surrendered possession to the superior Landlord that is nothing but a statement made by a person again 82 years without any link with the entire evidence as such the same cannot be construed as a complete evidence that possession was surrendered to the superior Landlord nor the same is an admission because his whole contention in the evidence is that upon taking joma and receiving rents he settled the suit property and delivered possession to the plaintiff. Whatever might be the statement of P.W.4 unless the provisions of sections 85, 86 and 87 of the B.T. Act are complied with the surrender cannot be proved under the law. The defendants having not taken any step to prove such surrender or abandonment of the Tenancy by Kunja Behari Ghose by adducing any evidence the allegation, of surrendering and or the statement made by Rashik Lal, will not ipso facto prove the defence case. 

 14. Mr. Nondy could not point out any misreading of evidence in the judgment of the lower appellate court for which the above principle laid down in 35 DLR could be attracted. The principle laid down in the 35 DLR case is not in revision under section 115 of the Code where the scope is very limited. But however, in the said decision it has also been observed "Misreading of evidence, not miss appreciation can be interfered with and partial misunderstanding of a document not a case for High Court's interference". Thus on this score also the above citation does not come for any assistance of the petitioner. On the contrary relying on the case of Md. Yasin and others Vs. Kamini Kumar Shome and others reported in 2 BCR 216 it can be said that mere payment of rent to the Government on the strength of unfounded entry in the record of rights will not create valid tenancy in favour of the defendants and extinguish the title, if any, of the plaintiffs. Thus Exhibit `A' series does not in any way help the defendants to prove their case.
